exposure: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) diagnosis with colchicine treatment
outcome: Maternal inflammatory markers (Neutrophil/Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR), Platelet/Lymphocyte Ratio (PLR), Monocyte/Lymphocyte Ratio (MLR))
cohort: The study included 42 pregnant women diagnosed with Familial Mediterranean Fever who were undergoing colchicine treatment and 126 healthy pregnant control women.
finding: Pregnant women with FMF receiving colchicine had significantly reduced hemoglobin levels, an elevated prevalence of anemia, diminished monocyte counts, and decreased MLR values compared to healthy controls, while other inflammatory markers, pregnancy complications, and neonatal outcomes were similar.
